Scope: what is in, and what is out

The project life cycle used in this book
Eight reasons student projects fail, and the cure

sections.title: What Project I is, and what it is not
Scope: what is in, and what is out
Feasibility: can this really be finished?
The project life cycle used in this book
Eight reasons student projects fail, and the cure

summary: A good Project I is small, finished and explained; it is judged on method, not size.
Ideas come from real problems; a funnel with three gates leaves one project.
The problem statement carries numbers; objectives are SMART; the scope table says what is out.
Feasibility is technical, economic, operational and schedule; a weighted score makes the decision.

units.title: Planning, Teamwork and Version Control
topics: Critical path: the tasks that cannot slip
Task boards, stand-ups and pair programming
Eight practices of a team that finishes

sections.title: Critical path: the tasks that cannot slip
Task boards, stand-ups and pair programming
Eight practices of a team that finishes

summary: A WBS with durations and dependencies gives a schedule; the critical path shows what cannot slip.
A Gantt chart shows the plan, a Kanban or Scrum board shows today.
Roles are shared but every member must know every module.
Git gives history, branches, merges and backup; main always works.

units.title: Analysis and Design: Requirements, DFD, ER and Screens
topics: Requirements: what the system must do
The ER diagram and the database schema
Eight benefits of designing before coding

sections.title: Requirements: what the system must do
The ER diagram and the database schema
Eight benefits of designing before coding

summary: Requirements are written as testable functional and non-functional statements.
Use-case diagrams show actors and functions; DFDs show data movement at level 0 and level 1.
The ER diagram becomes the schema; foreign keys protect the data (a real script proved it).
Wireframes and a design-first habit save weeks of rework and help in the viva.

units.title: Building and Testing: Code, Test Cases and Defects
topics: Defects and the bug life cycle
Eight reasons to test early and often

sections.title: Defects and the bug life cycle
Eight reasons to test early and often

summary: Separate screen, logic and data so that parts can be built and tested alone.
The CampusShelf logic layer runs: hashed login, 14-day loans, Rs 2 fines, overdue list.
Test cases are tied to requirements; unittest automates them (8 of 8 pass).
A bug log with steps to reproduce, severity and status keeps fixing organised.

units.title: The Report, the Presentation and the Viva
topics: The shape of a project report
Twelve viva questions, with model answers
Eight habits of a good viva

sections.title: The shape of a project report
Twelve viva questions, with model answers
Eight habits of a good viva

summary: The report mirrors the phases of the project; write each chapter when its phase ends.
Number figures and tables, use one reference style, and never copy without credit.
A ten-minute talk has about eight slides and a rehearsed demo with a backup.
In the viva, speak in numbers, explain from whole to part, admit limits and know every module.
